pr_title: Provide yeelight unique_id using ssdp discovery
pr_body:
## Proposed change
Add unique_id to yeelight component.

## Type of change
<!--

  NOTE: Please, check only 1! box!

- [X] New feature (which adds functionality to an existing integration)

## Additional information
Get unique_id from the device itself, using SSDP query to invidual device. Its implemented via new method from python-yeelight ( https://yeelight.readthedocs.io/en/latest/yeelight.html#yeelight.Bulb.get_capabilities ).
Query device once ( during initialization ) and then use cached capabilities.

pr_comments:
It's not mentioning ssdp in code here. Are you doing ssdp inside the lib? Is it listening or explicit requesting?

Just feels like a slippery slope to do ssdp stuff inside library. If all integration start doing it, well have a lot of broadcasts/listening sockets.

It uses this call: https://gitlab.com/stavros/python-yeelight/-/blob/master/yeelight/main.py#L244 during device init, and then reads cached values in unique_id method: https://gitlab.com/stavros/python-yeelight/-/blob/master/yeelight/main.py#L304 . Ive wrote about ssdp, as its the method used there, but its targeted to specific device. According to yeelight devs its supported this way. ( https://forum.yeelight.com/t/topic/12894/387 )
Fixed unique_id in inherited class ( nightlight / ambilight ) when unique id is not available for any reason.
Will this pull also fix https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/32493 ? Or would that need to be addressed differently?
No, this PR just removes the need to pass the model information manually, detecting bulbs requires another PR.
@rytilahti I think its done and ready for CR. Also maybe its not breaking change ?

Hmm, did you forget to commit/push? Here's what it shows as docstring for model:
```
"""Return configured device model.

Model method returns declared model, and if not, it tries to get it from
"""
```

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/35448/commits/fc6bceb4527922031ffa96f0b631e24a071fb8dd I've applied suggestion from you, looks like it was 1 line too short. Pushed rewrote as suggested in comment.
Sorry, my bad! I shouldn't have put it up as a suggestion... Let's merge it!

issue_context.body:

  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/

  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.

## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened instead.
-->
After the 0.106.5 update all my Yeelight color2 has been dissapeared. I was using the auto mode. Now with manual mode it is working again. But I would like to back to the auto mode.

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant release with the issue:  0.106.5
- Last working Home Assistant release (if known): 0.106.3
- Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.): Home Assistant (current name)
- Integration causing this issue: not sure about that discovery or yeelight
- Link to integration documentation on our website:  https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/discovery/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->
Not working config:
```yaml
discovery:
  ignore:
    - igd
```

Working config:
```yaml
discovery:
  ignore:
    - igd
    - homekit
    - yeelight

yeelight.yaml
devices:
  192.168.1.y:
    name: 'XXX'
  192.168.1.y:
    name: 'YYY'
```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```txt
There is no lines about that problem
```

## Additional information
I see everytime a notification about HomeKit not present in previous versions.
comments: Hey there @rytilahti, @zewelor, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`yeelight`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L417) for? Thanks!
I can replicate it in another hardware (the production one). Restoring to Home Assistant 0.106.3 it is enought for the Yeelight to start working again.
Same problem with my new HA installation (Raspberry), manual config works but I can't set fixed IPs (ISP wants DHCP disabled) (and Yeelight fw doesn't support static IP config)

Same issue with a CT light. With my color bulbs or color strips, I have not issue.
:-/

FYI I still have this issue with "Home Assistant 0.108.6" and I also have a weird notification to add Yeelight Strips to "HomeKit".

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12491721/79687364-0d8f3780-8247-11ea-8ebf-ceb857209c97.png)

Edit:  Went back to 0.100.1 and didn't work too .. :/

This issue is still present

Problem:
The bulb is auto-discovered as HomeKit device, but then I don't have a [HomeKit pin](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/homekit_controller) to pair it... This is not usable. The bulb should be auto-discovered directly, and if necessary show config option to choose version (white light, temperature light, color, strip...).

Only way to make it to work is by putting manual entry in config.yaml
If you have anything better than basic white lamp, you also need to go through docs to find correct model name string

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3856578/81290262-ad2e3180-905f-11ea-886d-27f3ae17b9a3.png)

I'm also having this issue as described by @Zireael 

@zewelor @rytilahti Will this get fixed by https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/35448 ?
That linked PR will allow automatic detection of the model, so that part of the problem will be fixed. Autodiscovering existing bulbs will require another PR.

> That linked PR will allow automatic detection of the model, so that part of the problem will be fixed. Autodiscovering existing bulbs will require another PR.

Thanks for the quick reply. Do you have any suggestions how we can move the autodiscovery forward?

The integration needs to be converted to use a config flow to do the detection. One of the blockers for that was the lack of an unique id, so that PR by @zewelor will allow proceeding to do that conversion.

Please make sure to update to the latest Home Assistant version and check if that solves the issue. Let us know if that works for you by adding a comment 👍
This issue now has been marked as stale and will be closed if no further activity occurs. Thank you for your contributions.
